value.rationale: The family Kpq is a canonical complete-bipartite graphical zonotope, and the natural isotropic spherical-width law changes from a finite-dimensional non-Gaussian functional to a Gaussian law precisely when the smaller part grows. The exact lower-edge exponent p/2 makes the small part geometrically identifiable, and the radial-projection covariance explains the strictly positive near-cancelled balanced fluctuation. These motivated angular-distribution invariants are not determined by known finite moments; the result does not claim new Hoeffding decomposition technology or require a separate paper-sized theorem.
